9/16/2026
**Dog was pulled and returned at same time as kennel mate, A5171346 but evaluated individually**
Handlers approached kennel front, dogs were laying on bed together. Lead handler knelt down and began offering treats, dogs were hesitant initially but dog up and began coming forward. Dogs remained tense and hesitant, handler tried to lure dog through loop with leash presented. Dog would back away when leash was presented. Handler stood up and was able to take a step in and place leash. Handler then held leash taut and scooped dog up with opposite hand. Handler was able to carry dog to M&G room. Dog was rigid in posture with legs fully extended. Once in M&G room alone handler adjusted leash stopper and released dog . Dog stayed away from handler initially, handler sat on chair towards back of room. Handler began offering treats, dog would approach for treats but would not take treats from handlers hands. About 5 minutes into evaluation dog approached handlers shoe and sniffed for a few seconds and then ate a few more treats from the ground. Dog then sat at opposite side of room and began ignoring handler. Handler continued to offer treats, dog ignored them. Handler tried to verbally coax dog would not look at handler. Handler allowed dog a few minutes and then retrieved leash. Handler again held leash taut and scooped up dog. Dog was rigid in posture and thrashed briefly then allowed carrying. 09/23/26 18:44
Ventral midline abdominal incision made with no. 15 blade. Patient's uterus and ovarian pedicles were found to be unusually tight and friable, suspect due to malnutrition and/or other underlying disease. Right ovarian pedicle tore during exteriorization, incision extended cranially to attempt to retrieve pedicle. Pedicle extremely friable and continue to tear during attempts at exteriorization. Continued on with remainder of surgery. Left ovarian pedicle double ligated with strangle knots using 2-0 Webmax. Ligated broad ligaments with simple circumferential ligatures using 2-0 Webmax. The uterine body tore during attempt at exteriorization, the incision was extended caudally to retrieve the the uterine body and it was ligated using two strangle knots using 2-0 Webmax. Reattempted exteriorizing right ovarian pedicle - unable as tissue was repeatedly tearing. Small amount of oozing noted in right gutter, but no significant hemorrhage. Abdomen lavaged with 1L warm LRS with 3mL gentamicin added. Placed small piece of gel foam in region of uterine body and placed large piece of gel foam in right guttter just caudal to right kidney in region of right ovarian pedicle. Observed for hemorrhage prior to closure. Body wall closed with cruciate and simple interrupted sutures using 0 Webmax. Subcutaneous tissue closed with simple continuous sutures using 2-0 Webmax. Skin closed with 3-0 Webmax in an intradermal pattern. Staples placed. Green tattoo etched. Applied tissue adhesive over abdominal incision and tattoo. Patient monitored serially post-operatively while running IV LRS at 20mL/hr. All vitals remained WNL and MM pink with CRT <2s. Recheck tomorrow AM to determine when patient will be okay for release. Plan to continue IV LRS tomorrow.

Immediate placement is needed with an experienced adopter or New Hope Partner who can provide time and space to decompress in a calm, supportive home. Placement needed by close of business 9/28/26. 09/24/26 14:07 This dog has demonstrated a persistent, recurring pattern of fluctuating in-kennel stress and anxiety, ranging from moderate to significant, over an extended period of time. These behaviors are often a response to the overwhelming sights, sounds, and confinement, along with the lack of choice or control over their environment. Although this dog continues to show appropriate behavior outside of the kennel with positive interactions with staff and volunteers, without intervention, well-being will continue to decline. Immediate placement is needed with an experienced adopter or New Hope Partner who can provide time and space to decompress in a calm, supportive home. Placement needed by close of business 9/29/26. May be at risk of euthanasia 9/30/26 or sooner if warranted.

sections.memo:
9/24/2026
09/24/26 14:08 This dog has demonstrated a persistent, recurring pattern of fluctuating in-kennel stress and anxiety, ranging from moderate to significant, over an extended period of time. These behaviors are often a response to the overwhelming sights, sounds, and confinement, along with the lack of choice or control over their environment. Although this dog continues to show appropriate behavior outside of the kennel with positive interactions with staff and volunteers, without intervention, well-being will continue to decline. Immediate placement is needed with an experienced adopter or New Hope Partner who can provide time and space to decompress in a calm, supportive home. Placement needed by close of business 9/29/26. May be at risk of euthanasia 9/30/26 or sooner if warranted.
Intake
3/19/2026
How long have you had the animal?
4 DAYS. DOG WAS ROAMING THE NEIGHBORHOOD, FINDER HAD PUT FOOD OUT AND WAS ABLE TO GET THE DOG TO GO INTO THEIR YARD.
Has the animal been around other animals? What kind of animals? How would you describe the interaction with other animals?
GOOD WITH FEMALE DOG IN HOME. PLAYFUL, TRIED TO MOUNT MULTIPLE TIMES. LOW GROWLS AT OTHER MALE DOG IN THE HOME.
Was the animal around any other people or children? If yes, how would you describe the animals behavior towards other people/children?
NO CONTACT WITH CHILDREN.
Has the animal shown any aggression around other people? Might want to include a few examples of what aggression looks like. Barking, growling, lunging, etc.? If yes, what were the circumstances?
GROWLS ON APPROACH, BUT WARMED UP QUICK.
Did you keep the animal inside or outside?
OUTSIDE
If inside, did you keep the animal in a crate or allowed to roam? Was the animal destructive in any way?
CRATE,CHEWED UP CRATE AND BEDDING. NO OTHER DESTRUCTION.
If outside, what kind of fencing do you have and did it contain the animal?
WOOD FENCE, YARD CONTAINED  DOG.
Did the animal show any aggression, like **growling, curling their lips, lunging** around food, toys, or bones?
GROWLED WHEN DOGS OR PEOPLE CAME NEAR ITS FOOD.
Has the animal shown any signs of illness?
NO SIGNS OF ILLNESS.
Does the animal walk on a leash?
PULLS HARD ON LEASH.

Dog was at front of kennel, neutral body, softly wagging tail at spine level, took treats gently through door,stayed at front gently pushing nose at opening as handler reached in to leash, jumped up once then allowed easy leash placement, moderate pull. Dog entered yard and began exploring, stopping to urine mark frequently and consistently throughout entire duration of evaluation. Dog had ears up and forward, still tail above spine level, alert, moving rapidly with darting motions around yard, sniffing and marking without acknowledging handlers, would brush past them while exploring yard, handlers sat on bench, call to dog, no response, handler used squeaker and dog immediately oriented toward sound, came up and sniffed squeaker then quickly walked away and resumed sniffing/marking. Handler would pet dog's back as he passed by, showed no reaction. As dog paced around yard, assistant picked up a ball and got his attention, would quickly chase it and retrieve it, dropping it and walking away but would reengage any time assistant offered ball. Handler would offer treats, dog showed no interest. On two occasions dog came up to assistant, not soliciting attention but allowed it briefly, stood facing away from them, softly panting, would continue to allow both handlers to pet in passing but did not engage with them. Dog was pacing yard and remained alert, panting heavier as evaluation continued. A dog barked in nearby kennel buildings, this dog ran up to the fence line with forward posture, tail and ears upright, stood at fence non reactive, then darted away. Walked to catch pen and allowed handler to pick up leash, strong pull, walked into kennel easily and removed leash by hand.
9/24/2026
Handlers approached kennel front, dog was excitable ,jumping up on glass, panting with dilated pupils. Handler offered some treats to help focus dog, handler was able to lure dog into loop through gate after a few attempts. Once leash was secure handler opened gate, dog exited kennel with lowered and rounded posture. Handler Guided dog to PY, dog was skittering on flooring and trying to dart through thresholds on path to PY. Once in PY handler attached leash extension, adjusted leash stopper and released dog. Dog kept to self for majority of the outing, minimal prosocial behavior. Dog paced perimeter of PY focusing mostly on exterior fence line. Dog would approach handlers when called and then immediately return to fence line, dog allowed brief petting in a drive by manner. Handlers allowed dog 5-10 minutes in PY, dog appeared to be increasing in FAS. Handler retrieved leash and placed clip leash. Dog pulled moderately on return, dog ignored occupied kennels in passing. Dog was hesitant to enter kennel but did so with light leash guidance. Handler used clip leash to remove leash and left behind jackpot of treats.
9/15/2026
Secured in finder's back patio. Finder stated dog was very friendly and calm yesterday, allowed her and a relative to carry him a mile to her home to wait for pick up; this morning, dog "flipped a switch" and became extremely aggressive towards her and her family.
I approached dog from inside of sliding glass door. Dog was laying but jumped up when he noticed me, full body was stiff, hair erect along all of back and tail, hard stare, growling, barking, and baring teeth. I reached to place hand near glass, and dog muzzle hit the glass hard where my hand was. I went to back gate to approach with restraint device, and dog sprinted from glass door to growl/bark at me through gate. Dog bit at device multiple times, and once secured on device, dog flailed a few times but stopped once I had gate open. Heavy flinching/skin crawl when I tried to brush hand on his shoulders, walked on device and was loaded onto truck with no further struggle.
9/15/2026
walks on leash, allows some dog handling, moderate restraint for vaccines, skittish, use caution when approaching and handling
